metadata.research_goal: Create backend-ready soccer role profiles for goalkeeper, center back, fullback/wingback, defensive midfielder, central midfielder, attacking midfielder, winger/wide forward, striker/center forward, and second striker/false nine, including phase responsibilities, physical demands, injury/load risks, and beginner/intermediate/advanced development implications.

key_concepts.title: Position is a phase-specific role, not a fixed spot
key_concepts.summary: A player can be a fullback on the team sheet but become an extra midfielder in build-up, a winger in sustained attack, or a back-five defender without the ball. Role records should store responsibilities by phase rather than by a single field coordinate.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use role plus phase maps in training generation and retrieval.

key_concepts.title: Every role needs four main phase responsibilities
key_concepts.summary: Profiles should describe attacking, defending, attacking transition, defensive transition, and set-piece tasks. The same technical skill has different value depending on the phase, for example a center-back pass in build-up versus a clearance under corner pressure.
key_concepts.backend_use: Normalize responsibilities into attacking, defensive, transition, and set-piece arrays.

key_concepts.title: The modern goalkeeper is both first attacker and box organizer
key_concepts.summary: Goalkeepers must protect the goal, dominate 1v1 and aerial situations, distribute under pressure with varied techniques, support goal-kick build-up, and organize teammates at set pieces.
key_concepts.backend_use: Goalkeeper plans should combine specialist handling/diving with team build-up and set-piece communication.

key_concepts.title: The central spine controls the team's risk
key_concepts.summary: Goalkeepers, center backs, defensive midfielders, and central midfielders repeatedly decide whether to secure possession, break a line, play over pressure, or delay and reorganize. Their errors often expose the most direct route to goal.
key_concepts.backend_use: Central role sessions should include scanning, body orientation, pressure recognition, and rest-defense decisions.

key_concepts.title: Wide roles work as partnerships
key_concepts.summary: Fullbacks/wingbacks and wingers/wide forwards share width, depth, 1v1 creation, overlapping and underlapping runs, counterpressing support, and wide defensive cover. Their responsibilities change when one player comes inside and the other stays wide.
key_concepts.backend_use: Generate paired wide-role drills rather than isolated winger or fullback drills only.

key_concepts.title: Midfielders need sub-role specificity
key_concepts.summary: Defensive midfielders protect central space and connect the first build-up pass, central midfielders connect phases and manage tempo, and attacking midfielders receive between lines to create or finish. All require scanning and body orientation, but their risk choices differ.
key_concepts.backend_use: Separate number 6, number 8, and number 10 priorities instead of using one generic midfielder record.

key_concepts.title: The front line starts the defense
key_concepts.summary: Wingers, center forwards, and second strikers influence pressing direction, screen central passes, trigger high regains, and prepare for immediate attacks after winning the ball. Their defensive load differs from deeper defenders because much of their high-speed work can be in possession or in pressing actions.
key_concepts.backend_use: Attacking role profiles should include pressing and counterpressing responsibilities.

key_concepts.title: A false nine only works with coordinated runners
key_concepts.summary: A false nine or second striker drops from a high starting point to receive and combine. The role creates value only if wide forwards, attacking midfielders, or a strike partner attack the spaces that defenders leave or hesitate to leave.
key_concepts.backend_use: False-nine records should include teammate dependencies and not be trained as isolated hold-up play.

key_concepts.title: Set pieces create specialist role assignments
key_concepts.summary: Corner and free-kick plans usually assign takers, aerial targets, screeners, blockers, near-post/far-post runners, zonal defenders, markers, edge players, counterattack outlets, and rest-defense players. These may differ from open-play responsibilities.
key_concepts.backend_use: Store set-piece responsibility fields for each role rather than assuming open-play tasks apply.

key_concepts.title: Physical demands are shaped by role, style, and match context
key_concepts.summary: Central and defensive midfielders often cover large total distances, wide roles and attackers carry more high-speed and sprint work, and center backs typically show lower running volumes but high duel, jump, and recovery-sprint demands. Tactical style can move a player away from broad positional averages.
key_concepts.backend_use: Scale conditioning prescriptions by role and team model rather than by generic soccer fitness.

key_concepts.title: Injury risk follows role exposure patterns
key_concepts.summary: High-speed running, repeated accelerations, aerial duels, heading exposure, tackles, dives, kicking volume, and congested match calendars create different risk profiles. Position labels help but should be combined with actual workload history and prior injury.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use role risk tags as defaults and adjust with player load, minutes, age, and injury history.

key_concepts.title: Role development progresses from literacy to adaptation
key_concepts.summary: Beginners need simple field reference points, body shape, communication, and core skills. Intermediate players add scanning, timing, phase transitions, and role partnerships. Advanced players adapt role behavior to opponent, formation, score, and match state.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create level-specific role objectives for beginner, intermediate, and advanced training plans.

technical_models.title: Phase-role matrix
technical_models.application: Use the matrix to generate sessions that train the role's job in a specific phase, such as fullback defensive transition after an overlap or striker first press after a lost pass.

technical_models.title: Position numbering and role groups
technical_models.application: Use numbering as a coaching shorthand while allowing role variations by formation and tactical instruction.

technical_models.title: Goal-kick distribution framework

model.around_and_support: short support passes to goalkeeper or center backs
model.through: passes into central midfield or a player between pressure lines
model.into: passes into wider or higher fullback areas
model.onto: passes into a center forward or target for hold-up and second balls
model.beyond: passes into space behind the defensive line

technical_models.application: Goalkeeper, center-back, fullback, midfielder, and forward profiles should all include their receiving or supporting jobs in each distribution option.

technical_models.title: Rest-defense and counterattack protection model

model.front_of_ball: attackers and advanced midfielders counterpress or delay
model.around_ball: nearest players press, cover, and block forward lanes
model.behind_ball: center backs, defensive midfielders, and weak-side fullback protect central depth and counterattack outlets

technical_models.application: Use after attacking actions such as fullback overlap, corner, or attacking-midfielder dribble to decide who protects the team if possession is lost.

technical_models.title: Wide-channel rotation model

model.outside_width: one wide player pins the touchline or final-line width
model.inside_lane: one player moves into half-space to receive, combine, or underlap
model.overlap_or_underlap: timed run from deeper player creates a crossing or cutback option
model.cover_balance: midfielder or center back shifts to protect behind the run

technical_models.application: Use for fullback/wingback and winger/wide-forward pair sessions.

technical_models.title: Midfield receiving model

model.scan: identify pressure, teammate angles, and forward options before receiving
model.body_shape: receive side-on where possible to access both directions
model.first_touch: set the next action away from pressure
model.risk_choice: play forward, switch, secure, or bounce based on pressure and team balance

technical_models.application: Use for defensive, central, and attacking midfield progression with different risk thresholds.

technical_models.title: Forward reference and runner model

model.target_reference: holds off defender, sets the ball, contests aerials, and connects runners
model.depth_runner: threatens space behind the defensive line and times curved runs
model.box_finisher: arrives in high-value scoring spaces and attacks rebounds
model.false_nine: drops away from center backs to link play and create room for runners

technical_models.application: Distinguish striker/center forward from second striker/false nine while allowing hybrid plans.

technical_models.title: Corner-defense assignment model

model.zonal: players protect spaces and attack the ball in assigned zones
model.player_to_player: players track assigned opponents and deny first contact or shots
model.hybrid: zonal protectors combine with individual markers and edge players
model.goalkeeper: sets starting position, sees the ball, organizes, claims or punches when feasible
model.outlet_and_rest_defense: selected players protect edge spaces or prepare counterattack

technical_models.application: Set-piece training should allocate role-specific jobs before rehearsing delivery, first contact, second phase, and exit.

technical_models.title: Role development ladder

model.beginner: understand shape, reference points, simple decisions, and safe technique
model.intermediate: execute under pressure, scan earlier, time runs, combine with partners, and recover after actions
model.advanced: adapt to opponent, formation, game state, and tactical plan while sustaining match-speed physical output

technical_models.application: Use the ladder in all role_skill_priority and role_training_implication records.

tactical_rules.rule: The goalkeeper should choose distribution by pressure, teammate spacing, and opponent structure, not by a fixed short-or-long preference.
coaching_cues: mix short support with direct balls onto or beyond the front line

tactical_rules.rule: Goalkeeper hand use is a specialist advantage only inside the penalty area and only within the Laws; back-pass, throw-in, release, and outside-area situations must be trained as decision constraints.
A center back steps in only when cover and pressure make the action safe; otherwise they protect depth, track runners, and keep the route to goal closed.
When the opponent's press blocks normal passing lanes, center backs can break the first line with a carry or direct forward pass, but only if the rest-defense shape behind the ball is stable.
A fullback or wingback should provide width, overlap, underlap, or inverted support according to the winger's position and the team's counterattack cover.
coaching_cues: arrive on timing not too early
recover immediately if the ball is lost

tactical_rules.rule: The defensive midfielder protects central access before chasing wide pressure, especially when fullbacks advance or center backs split.
coaching_cues: screen pass into striker or number 10
turn pressure into predictable wide play

tactical_rules.rule: Central midfielders should scan before receiving and shape their body to play forward, switch, or secure the ball based on pressure.
coaching_cues: one or two touch when central pressure is high

tactical_rules.rule: The attacking midfielder should arrive between lines on the blind side of midfield pressure, receive on the half-turn when possible, and connect quickly to runners or shots.
coaching_cues: move after defender looks at the ball
play third-player or final pass quickly

tactical_rules.rule: A winger or wide forward should stretch the back line when width is needed, attack 1v1 when isolated, combine with the fullback when doubled, and recover to deny penetrations in wide areas.
coaching_cues: track the opposing fullback after turnovers

tactical_rules.rule: The center forward should give the team a reference point by threatening behind, holding up when direct play is needed, attacking crosses, and leading the first press.
When a false nine drops, at least one teammate should threaten the vacated depth so center backs cannot simply hold their line and allow free reception.
After regaining the ball, players should scan for exposed spaces before the regain, then play forward quickly when a clear advantage exists or secure possession if the team is unbalanced.
coaching_cues: support below and beyond the ball

tactical_rules.rule: After losing possession, the nearest players press or delay while deeper players protect central depth and counterattack lanes.
Attacking set pieces should assign takers, aerial targets, blockers, rebound players, and rest-defense cover before rehearsing the delivery.
Defensive corners should define whether each player is zonal, player-to-player, edge, post, goalkeeper-protection, or outlet, and should include second-phase exits.
Penalty moments separate the kicker-goalkeeper duel from other players' rebound responsibilities; both should be trained with legal starting positions and psychological routine.
coaching_cues: all others prepare rebound and clearance lanes

physical_demands.summary: Low running volume compared with outfield roles, but high reactive demand: explosive dives, short accelerations, jumps, contact landings, kicking and throwing, 1v1 spread saves, and repeated cognitive resets.

Usually lower total and high-speed running than many outfield roles, but high demand for aerial duels, contact strength, backward/sideways movement, recovery sprints, box defending, and line-breaking passes or carries.
Wide defenders and wingbacks carry large repeated high-speed loads through overlaps, underlaps, defensive recovery runs, wide 1v1s, accelerations, decelerations, and crossing actions.
High total distance with frequent out-of-possession positioning, short accelerations, decelerations, duels, screening movements, and passing under central pressure.
Typically among the highest total-distance roles, with repeated support angles, pressing, recovery, turns, short accelerations, and limited recovery between high-intensity efforts.
Mixed creative and pressing load: repeated movements between lines, sharp accelerations and decelerations, turns under pressure, dribble contacts, final-pass actions, and immediate counterpressing.
High-speed and sprint-heavy profile with 1v1 acceleration, repeated wide runs, diagonal runs behind, pressing, defensive recovery, crossing, cutbacks, and shooting after high-speed actions.
Explosive and contact-heavy demand: curved runs, short sprints behind, pressing, hold-up collisions, aerial contests, box accelerations, and high-pressure finishing.
Hybrid forward-midfield demand: repeated checks away from the back line, turns between lines, wall passes, short accelerations, pressing from central lanes, and late box arrivals.

Set pieces add jump, landing, grappling, blocking, sprint-to-mark, kicking, and second-ball collision load. Center backs, strikers, and goalkeepers are often exposed to the highest aerial and contact dose.
Position-specific conditioning should combine physical outputs with tactical actions, because match running and explosive actions depend on the role's decisions, not only on distance covered.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Hamstring strain risk rises with high-speed sprint exposure, rapid accelerations, fatigue, prior injury, and poorly progressed return to sprinting.
Cutting, tackling, repeated changes of direction, wide defensive recovery, and kicking can load the hip and adductor complex.
1v1 attacking, defensive changes of direction, tackles, and high-speed decelerations create ankle sprain and knee load risk.

Repeated heading, aerial duels, and corner/free-kick collisions expose players to acute head injury risk and possible long-term head-impact concerns, with defenders especially relevant in long-career data.
mitigation: limit unnecessary repetitive heading in youth

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Goalkeepers face hand/finger trauma, shoulder load, hip/lumbar stress, contact at feet, and landing load from dives and aerial claims.
Center backs may have lower running volumes but high contact, tackling, jumping, backward movement, and emergency sprint exposures that can create soft-tissue, ligament, and collision risk.
Midfield roles can accumulate high total distance, accelerations, decelerations, duels, and cognitive load across both possession phases.
Set pieces concentrate crowding, blocks, aerial challenges, second-ball tackles, and goalkeeper traffic, increasing collision and landing-risk moments.
Some injury literature suggests forwards may have higher match injury risk, but findings are mixed and should be treated as a monitoring cue rather than a deterministic rule.
Repeated one-sided kicking, crossing, shooting, and long distribution can create hip, adductor, abdominal, lumbar, or lower-limb asymmetry issues.
mitigation: avoid large extra technical volumes after match load

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Youth players may be vulnerable when growth, new field sizes, early specialization, sudden minutes increases, and adult-like role loads arrive at the same time.
mitigation: avoid treating academy position averages as fixed targets

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Central roles make repeated high-consequence decisions under pressure; fatigue can increase scanning errors, poor body shape, late recovery, and unsafe central turnovers.

training_implications.summary: Design role sessions around one phase and one tactical problem, such as fullback overlap-to-recovery, defensive midfielder screen-to-switch, or striker press-to-finish.
training_implications.backend_use: Session generator should request role, phase, opponent behavior, and success cue.

training_implications.summary: Goalkeepers should train with the team for build-up, goal-kick choices, defensive line connection, and set-piece organization, not only isolated shot-stopping.
training_implications.backend_use: Include goalkeeper as active player in build-up and transition sessions when the role is present.

training_implications.summary: Conditioning should respect role outputs: midfield repeatability, wide high-speed exposure, striker acceleration/contact, center-back duel and recovery sprinting, and goalkeeper power/landing.
training_implications.backend_use: Map role to default conditioning themes and adjust by player workload.

training_implications.summary: Beginners should experience multiple roles before specialization so they understand width, depth, support angles, defensive compactness, and transitions.
training_implications.backend_use: Beginner plans should include role rotation and universal principles before heavy sub-role specialization.

training_implications.summary: Midfield development should progress from unopposed body shape and scanning to opposed receiving, pressure from blind side, and tactical risk choices.
training_implications.backend_use: Midfielder plans should include scan-before-receive constraints and one-touch/two-touch variations.

training_implications.summary: Fullback/wingback and winger/wide-forward should train as a pair for overlap, underlap, isolation, counterpress, and recovery coverage.
training_implications.backend_use: Generate two-role unit drills for wide-channel actions.

training_implications.summary: Second-striker and false-nine sessions should include coordinated runners, not just receiving drills, because the role depends on how teammates exploit vacated spaces.
training_implications.backend_use: Require at least one depth runner and one support player in false-nine drill templates.

training_implications.summary: Set-piece sessions should identify exact jobs before repetition: taker, target, blocker, screener, rebound player, zonal defender, marker, edge player, goalkeeper, and outlet.
training_implications.backend_use: Set-piece records should include role assignment and first/second-phase cues.

training_implications.summary: Wide players, forwards, and attacking midfielders need progressive sprint, acceleration, and deceleration exposure across the week to prepare for match-speed actions without sudden spikes.
training_implications.backend_use: Auto-add sprint/deceleration monitoring prompts for high-speed roles.

training_implications.summary: Aerial roles need heading technique, neck/trunk strength, landing skill, and exposure management, with extra caution for youth and anyone with head-injury history.
training_implications.backend_use: Add heading volume and concussion-safety notes to center-back, striker, and set-piece plans.

training_implications.summary: Return-to-play should match the role's actual exposures: a winger may need near-max sprint and deceleration reintroduction, a center back needs aerial/contact and recovery sprints, and a goalkeeper needs diving/landing and distribution volume.
training_implications.backend_use: Injury return templates should be role-tagged rather than generic soccer only.

training_implications.summary: Advanced role development should include opponent-specific adaptations such as playing over the press, changing winger/fullback rotations, choosing when the center back carries, or deciding whether the false nine drops or pins.
training_implications.backend_use: Advanced plans should include opponent model and match-state constraints.

backend_records_to_create.role_summary: Specialist who protects the goal, controls the penalty area, distributes to start attacks, supports build-up under pressure, and organizes defensive set pieces.

attacking: choose short, through, wide, target, or space-behind distribution
switch play with feet or throw when available
defensive: sweep behind the defensive line when appropriate
attacking_transition: release counterattack quickly when advantage exists
secure possession if team is stretched
defensive_transition: decide stay, sweep, or delay in 1v1
set_pieces: claim or punch within feasible range

backend_records_to_create.role_summary: Central defender who protects the goal, leads defensive organization, wins duels, controls depth, and increasingly starts build-up through passing or carries.

attacking: split or support goalkeeper in build-up
play through, around, or over pressure
defensive: mark or pass on center forward
set_pieces: primary aerial target or blocker in attack
zonal or player-to-player defender in own box

backend_records_to_create.role_summary: Wide defender who balances flank defending with attacking width, overlaps, underlaps, inverted support, crossing, counterpressing, and recovery runs.

attacking: provide width or invert as instructed
support rest defense when opposite side attacks
defensive: compact inside when ball is opposite
attacking_transition: deliver early cross when advantage exists
defensive_transition: communicate cover with center back and defensive midfielder
set_pieces: possible taker from wide free kicks or corners

backend_records_to_create.role_summary: Number 6 who screens the back line, balances attacking structure, receives under pressure, connects build-up, and protects central counterattack lanes.

attacking: show between or beside center backs
defensive: screen passes into striker and number 10
defensive_transition: stop counterattack before back line is exposed

backend_records_to_create.role_summary: Number 8 link player who connects defense and attack, supports both sides of the ball, manages tempo, presses, and arrives into advanced spaces.

attacking_transition: play first forward pass or carry

backend_records_to_create.role_summary: Number 10 who receives between lines, creates chances, combines around the box, presses central exits, and links midfield with forwards.

defensive: press center backs or midfielders as system requires
attacking_transition: turn regain into through ball or carry

backend_records_to_create.role_summary: Wide attacker who provides width or diagonal threat, beats defenders 1v1, creates crosses and cutbacks, attacks the far post, and helps press and defend the flank.

defensive: support own fullback in wide areas
set_pieces: back-post attacker or defender depending on size

backend_records_to_create.role_summary: Primary central forward who scores, occupies center backs, attacks depth and crosses, holds play when direct, and initiates the first defensive pressure.

attacking: pin or separate from center backs
defensive: defend front zone on set-piece exits

backend_records_to_create.role_summary: Hybrid forward who links between midfield and attack, drops to create overloads, combines around a striker or as a withdrawn number 9, and creates space for runners.

attacking: play wall passes and through balls
defensive: help trap play toward one side

intermediate: use both feet under light pressure

advanced: break lines by pass or carry

beginner: defend the line and inside channel
advanced: choose overlap, underlap, invert, or hold
adapt to opponent winger and press
change role between 6, 8, and 10 tasks as game requires
rotate with false nine or winger
read when to isolate or combine
alternate false nine and box threat based on opponent

backend_records_to_create.demand_summary: Explosive, reactive, and technical-load role with low running volume but high dive, jump, landing, handling, throwing, kicking, and communication load.
Lower average running profile than many outfield roles but high duel, jump, contact, backpedal, turn, and emergency recovery sprint demand.
High-speed, repeated-sprint, acceleration/deceleration, and wide 1v1 role with frequent transitions from attack to recovery defense.
High total distance and repeated short-action role with central duels, screening shifts, pressure receiving, and transition protection.
Large total-distance and repeat-effort role connecting both penalty areas through support runs, pressing, recovery, and repeated turns.
Explosive, high-decision role with repeated checks between lines, turns, dribbles, counterpressing, and final-action efforts.
Sprint-heavy and repeated 1v1 role with high-speed runs, explosive changes of direction, pressing, recovery, and final-third delivery.
Short explosive and contact role with sprints behind, curved pressing, hold-up duels, aerial contests, and finishing actions.
Hybrid mobility role with midfielder-like turning and passing plus forward-like acceleration, pressing, and finishing bursts.

primary_risks: hip and lumbar stress from kicking and diving
ankle sprain from contact in tight spaces

session_design: rehearse corners with goalkeeper sight-line and timing
aerial duel technique with controlled contact

advanced: coordinate rotations with winger and midfielder
adapt as 6 or 10 when rotation requires
maintain quality at high running load

session_design: third-player passing circuits to opposed play

advanced: adapt to direct or possession game plan
coordinate runner ecosystem against opponent shape

session_design: false-nine drop with winger depth runs
